exposure: Pre-gestational iodine intake (<150 µg/day vs ≥150 µg/day)
outcome: Maternal-fetal adverse events (composite outcome including gestational diabetes, prematurity, caesarean sections, and newborns large/small for gestational age)
cohort: 2523 normoglycemic pregnant women with data on pre-gestational food-based iodine consumption
finding: Reaching the recommended pre-gestational iodine intake of ≥150 µg/day through food consumption was associated with lower rates of hypothyroxinemia, miscarriage, and a composite of maternal-fetal adverse events.
mod_finding: Reaching the recommended pre-gestational iodine intake of ≥150 µg/day was associated with a lower rate of caesarean sections.
